Non-building locations.question: For locations without a real street address (parks, trailheads, port-a-potties), what should the submitter enter instead of a street address?
Non-building locations.answer: Free-text location description replaces the address field when there's no street address (e.g. "North parking lot restroom, Alton Baker Park").

Non-building locations.question: Does this need a distinct "location type" dimension (e.g. Park/Outdoor vs Business Interior), separate from policy_tag?
Non-building locations.answer: No new field — the existing "Public Facility" policy tag already covers these adequately.

Non-building locations.question: Should non-building locations get distinct map pin/icon treatment (e.g. a different marker for a port-a-potty vs. a business)?
Non-building locations.answer: No, same pin styling as everything else for now — defer icon variety to a later polish phase.

Non-building locations.question: For non-building entries, should Google Places autocomplete stay active, or should there be an explicit "skip autocomplete / describe the location" affordance?
Non-building locations.answer: Explicit skip affordance — a small "No address? Describe the location instead" link/toggle switches the field from Places-autocomplete mode to a plain free-text field.

Non-building locations.question: Should the address/description text ever be geocoded to derive the pin's coordinates, or does the live GPS fix from Step 3 always provide the canonical coordinates regardless of what's typed in the address field?
Non-building locations.answer: GPS is always canonical — the address/description is a human-readable label only; the real lat/lng always comes from the submitter's live GPS fix at Step 3 (matches the "physically present" requirement). No geocoding dependency.
